_comment: The only hand-edited input to the generated artwork. See DESIGN.md.
_theme: Identity, in one place. KDE wants it in three metadata files and the installer wants it in a Go const; all four are written from here so they cannot drift.

theme.name: Vanilla Box Dark
theme.author: Sizwe
theme.description: A minimal, modern look — dark variant

_foreground: Text does not follow the tint. Warm text on a blue surface reads as a mistake rather than a variant, and holding it still keeps every tint recognisably the same theme.
_surfaces: Hand-tuned per set rather than derived: a computed hue shift misbehaves at the lightness of the view background, which is also why tooltip is written out per set rather than taken as a percentage of view — at this lightness a multiplier collapses the sets into each other and the tint stops being legible. Named separately from the palettes so a set can be shared, and so a palette can be renamed without renaming the colours it points at.
_palettes: A palette is a surface set and the accent that goes with it, chosen together so the two never have to be reconciled by the user. A tinted accent matches its surfaces in temperature, so the variant reads as one decision, not two; neutral and slate take a grey accent instead, leaving the tint to the surfaces alone. An accent is also the selection background, so how dark it goes decides which foreground can sit on top of it. Every palette here takes the shared dark onHighlight; a palette whose accent is dark enough to need the light one can override it with its own onHighlight.
_shape: The theme rounds, and that is not a preference. Corners come from one small scale rather than a radius tuned per component: 10 for the surfaces — the titlebar, the panel strip, and the popups and applet backgrounds that are surfaces in their own right — and 8 for what sits on one: tooltips, buttons, inputs and list items. Two values shared across the theme is what makes the corners read as one system. The three maps stay keyed by a shape name because the renderers are written against one, and because a radius of 0 is still what a corner builder does with a square: nothing here forbids adding a shape back, but none ships.
_decorationShadow: Breeze's window shadow, reproduced. Breeze is a native KDecoration3 plugin: kdecoration/breezedecoration.cpp renders a QImage with BoxShadowRenderer and hands it to the compositor via DecorationShadow, which Aurorae has no API for. What it renders is two Gaussian-blurred rounded boxes composited over one another, and a blurred edge has a closed form, so the same field is drawn here as gradients in Aurorae's padding band. These are the s_shadowParams entries for ShadowSmall. Breeze ships ShadowLarge, but a nine-slice cannot carry it: a Gaussian's corner needs about 3*sigma of FIXED tile to settle in, Large's sigma is 24 so it wants 72px, and the titlebar row that has to hold it is 30px. Small's sigma is 8, wanting 21px, which fits. The values are otherwise Breeze's own, taken the same way, with ShadowStrength 255 and ShadowColor 0,0,0 from breezesettingsdata.kcfg. offsetY and each layer's offsetY are Breeze's QPoint offsets; overlap is Metrics::Shadow_Overlap. Padding is not written here: it is derived exactly as createShadowObject derives it, from the blur extents.
_popupShadow: The shadow under the launcher and the system tray popups: a single blurred box the shape of the popup, shrunk inset pixels inside the popup's outline on every side and then pushed down offsetY pixels, at strength opacity where it has settled. It started as Breeze's own popup shadow (strength 0.25, radius 6, offsetY 2), which was invisible in use: the popups usually open over dark windows about their own brightness, where a quarter-strength shadow darkens the backdrop by four levels. These values darken it by about 8 at the popup's side and 10 below it, and reach about three times as far; the inset keeps most of that below the popup rather than around it. radius is Breeze's blur radius, stdDev = radius/2. The tiles, their margins and the part cut out under the popup are all derived from these and the popup's corner radius.
_buttonStyles: Two treatments, not one with different values. Glyph buttons show a symbol always and gain a plate on hover; circle buttons show no symbol ever and gain colour on hover. Traffic-light colours are muted: authentic macOS values would be the most saturated pixels in the theme by a wide margin. Sizes were tuned by eye against a real titlebar: glyphSize is in rendered pixels, circleRadius is in 24x24 tile units and so scales with the button box. TestTitlebarButtonMetrics pins both.
_opacity: How much of what is behind a surface comes through it. Zero and one both mean opaque and emit no fill-opacity at all. tooltipBorder is the odd one and is not a surface's opacity at all: it is how much of the foreground colour the tooltip's outline lays over its own edge. The outline goes through the stylesheet rather than a literal, so a palette cannot bake its own border in — which means the number here is the only control over how far the edge separates from the surface. Low, because the surface under it is nearly black and a tenth of the text colour was already reading as a lit rim rather than an edge.
